basics.name: Mecapedia: Enciclopedia de Ingenieria Mecanica (Universitat Jaume I)
basics.resource_type: encyclopedia/wiki (university-authored online encyclopedia, not openly editable; readers report errors through a Google Form on the Contact page)
basics.license: Footer reads '(c) Area de Ingenieria Mecanica. Universitat Jaume I' with a disclaimer that the named authors alone are responsible for content. No Creative Commons or other open licence was found on the pages opened, so treat text as all rights reserved: link to it freely, but do not copy text or images without permission [uncertain]
basics.language: Spanish only (occasional English equivalents in brackets, e.g. 'backlash', 'torque limiter')
basics.year: Started 2006 by lecturers of the Mechanical Engineering Area, Universitat Jaume I (stated on the home page); page database shows the latest entry update on 6 March 2025 (friction-wheel drive catalogue page). Site rebuilt on Bootstrap 5 with a new JavaScript animation library; in 2024 it won the Federacion Iberoamericana de Ingenieria Mecanica 'Francisco Alba Juez' prize for best publication
basics.image_license: Mixed: the authors' own photos and diagrams (covered by the university copyright footer) plus some Wikimedia Commons images credited in captions (e.g. the backlash diagram credited to Slashme on Commons). The animations are the authors' own SVG/JavaScript code. No open licence stated for the site's own images [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: educator (university lecturers; each page names its author, e.g. Antonio Perez, Jose V. Garcia, Marta C. Mora; not peer-reviewed)

coverage.covers: University-level mechanical engineering topics: machine elements (keys, pins, cams, springs, belts, screws), systems (couplings, bearings, gear trains, belt/chain/cable drives, ball screws, power screws), classic planar linkages (four-bar, six-bar Watt and Stephenson, straight-line linkages, quick-return, Scotch yoke, pantograph), plus concepts, phenomena (friction, fatigue, irreversibility/self-locking, backlash), laws, models, parameters and procedures. The page database (db.js) lists 304 pages: 63 systems, 62 concepts, 40 models, 37 elements, 27 phenomena, 24 catalogue pages, 21 procedures, 16 parameters, 9 laws, 3 standards pages, 2 lessons; 40 pages carry animations
coverage.organisation: A side menu of content-type categories (Concepts, Elements, Phenomena, Lessons, Laws, Models, Parameters, Procedures, Systems), plus 'Everything' (A-Z list), 'Random page', 'Animations', 'Nomenclature' (symbol list for formulas), 'Catalogues', 'Standards', 'Calculators' and a search box. Each category page is an alphabetical list of titles. Grouping by content type (element vs system vs concept) is a textbook idea that does not help a beginner who is looking for 'something that does X'; you need to already know the Spanish term
coverage.scope_match: medium: covers many in-scope mechanism and transmission TYPES (gear trains, planetary, worm, cams, Scotch yoke, straight-line linkages, dwell mechanisms, Oldham coupling, self-locking screws), but it is a general mechanical-engineering course encyclopedia in Spanish with nothing on snap fits, print-in-place, compliant joints, powered latches or adhesives, and its Catalogues section is a list of links to manufacturers' catalogues (the standard-hardware kind of resource the project leaves out)
coverage.taxonomy_used: Two schemes. (1) Site-wide: 11 content-type categories (Conceptos, Elementos, Fenomenos, Lecciones, Leyes, Modelos, Parametros, Procedimientos, Sistemas, Catalogos, Estandares). (2) The Catalogues page source still holds an older, commented-out functional classification of machine components with 14 top-level groups: raw materials; actuators (manual, pneumatic, electric motors, hydraulic, vibrators); material feeding; shafts and axles; joining parts with no degrees of freedom (screws, washers, nuts, pins, rivets, keys, taper bushes, clamps); joining parts by simple kinematic pairs (rotary guides/bearings, linear guides, wheels, ball joints, couplings); transmission systems of several pairs (belt, chain, gear, ball screw, power screw, cable, linear actuators); elastic, damping and anti-vibration elements; brakes, clutches and torque limiters (freewheels, disc and drum brakes, fluid couplings, torque limiters); automation elements; complex transmission systems; machine safety; machines; maintenance (tools, seals, lubricants)
coverage.example_types: Oldham coupling (acoplamiento de Oldham); sleeve coupling (acoplamiento de manguito); Scotch yoke (mecanismo de yugo escoces), in 4-link and 3-link pin-in-slot forms; dwell / intermittent-motion six-bar (mecanismo con movimiento intermitente); Whitworth quick-return mechanism; Chebyshev, Hoekens, Peaucellier, Roberts and Watt straight-line linkages; pantograph; planetary / epicyclic gear train (tren de engranajes planetarios); worm gear (engranaje de tornillo sinfin); rack and pinion (transmision por pinon-cremallera); friction-wheel drive (transmision por rueda de friccion); ball screw (husillo de bolas); power screw / lead screw (tornillo de potencia); Woodruff key (chaveta Woodruff); cam types: plate, wedge, ribbed cylindrical, grooved cylindrical and face cams; cable drive (transmision por cable); taper locking bush (buje conico de fijacion, catalogue only); torque limiter (limitador de par, catalogue only); fluid coupling (acoplamiento hidraulico, catalogue only)
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering / machine design (industrial machinery); nothing specific to 3D printing, CNC or hobby robotics
coverage.item_count: 304 pages in the site database (about 280 encyclopedia entries plus 24 catalogue pages); 40 pages with animations
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Self-locking: yes, a dedicated 'Irreversibilidad' (irreversibility) entry explains why worm gears and power screws cannot be back-driven and that this is used as a safety feature in hoists. Gear trains/gearboxes: yes (ordinary and planetary gear trains, worm, bevel, helical, rack and pinion, speed reducers and multipliers). Indexing/dwell: partly, via the intermittent-motion six-bar linkage (no Geneva drive entry found). Torque-limiting: only as a Catalogues page linking to manufacturers' friction and ball-detent torque limiters (Cotransa, Boston Gear, R+W); no explanatory entry. One-way/ratchet: freewheels (ruedas libres) appear only in the old commented-out catalogue list, with no page. Over-centre, hand-release only, compliant, print-in-place, powered connectors (electromagnets, solenoid latches) and adhesives: not covered (electric motors appear only as catalogue link pages) [uncertain]
coverage.entry_structure: Title, category badge, author, last-modified date, a short definition paragraph, photos or diagrams with captions, formulas (MathJax) in analysis pages, SVG/JavaScript animations on 40 pages, and an automatic 'see also' list of linked entries. Catalogue pages are a table: company, links to its web page and PDF catalogues, and a one-line description (e.g. 'friction torque limiter', 'ball torque limiter')
coverage.audience_level: undergraduate (engineering students), also useful to professionals

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: short, clear definitions with photos and animations, but written in Spanish textbook language that assumes engineering vocabulary (kinematic pair, link, transmission angle), and there is no plain-language entry point
usefulness.has_images: yes: photos of real parts and simple diagrams on many element/system pages; quality is decent but small and uneven, some pages have no images
usefulness.has_animations: yes: 40 pages have interactive-looking SVG animations drawn in the browser by the site's own JavaScript library (e.g. four-bar, slider-crank, Scotch yoke, straight-line linkages, cam and follower, internal and external gears)
usefulness.gaps: Spanish only; no plain-English or beginner layer; no function-based or 'what do you need to do' navigation; nothing on 3D printing, snap fits, print-in-place, compliant mechanisms, clever everyday connectors, powered latches or adhesives; torque limiters and freewheels have no explanatory pages; no design rules for printed parts; no downloadable CAD
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes: each entry has a stable, readable per-page URL, e.g. https://www.mecapedia.uji.es/pages/mecanismo_de_yugo_escoces.html (Scotch yoke) or https://www.mecapedia.uji.es/pages/irreversibilidad.html (self-locking). Useful as a Spanish-language 'further reading' link
usefulness.reusable_data: scrape-only, but easy: the whole page index is one JavaScript file (https://www.mecapedia.uji.es/db/db.js) holding a JSON object of every page with title, author, category, has-animation flag and last-modified date. No licence is given for reusing the list or text, so link to it rather than copying [uncertain]
usefulness.maintained: yes: online and updated (latest page date 6 March 2025 in db.js; 2024 award noted on the home page). The legacy index URL http://www.mecapedia.uji.es/indices.htm now returns 403, so old deep links may be broken. Wayback Machine could not be checked from this environment
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) One small JSON 'database' file listing every entry with category, author, date and an 'animated' flag, which drives all index pages; a good lightweight model for the encyclopedia. (2) An 'Animations' index that lists only the entries with moving diagrams. (3) A 'Random page' button for browsing. (4) Keeping 'explanatory entry' and 'where to buy it (catalogues)' as separate linked pages, so the explanation stays brand-neutral. (5) The old functional catalogue tree (joints with no freedom / joints with one freedom / transmissions / elastic elements / brakes, clutches and torque limiters) is a usable top-level grouping idea. (6) An 'Irreversibility' concept page that ties several mechanisms together by behaviour
usefulness.design_rules_given: Some: Calculators page links to Google Sheets for spring pre-design, leaf springs, transverse pin strength, torsion bars, stress concentration and fatigue limits; Standards pages summarise standard dimensions for keys, Woodruff keys and pins. Nothing on 3D-print clearances, snap-fit strain or torque settings
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No geometry generators; the Calculators are Google Sheets for sizing (springs, pins, shafts). The animations are parametric SVG code but not offered as a tool
usefulness.file_formats: HTML pages, SVG/JavaScript animations, JPG/PNG images, links to manufacturers' PDF catalogues, Google Sheets calculators
usefulness.terminology_value: high for Spanish: a good source for correct Spanish names of mechanisms and machine elements (e.g. yugo escoces, tornillo de potencia, rueda libre, limitador de par) when adding translations or aliases; English equivalents are only given occasionally
usefulness.decision_support: None: no selector, flow chart, filters or comparison tables; only category lists, search, random page and cross-links between entries
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Original content written by UJI lecturers; draws on standard machine-design textbooks and uses some Wikimedia Commons images. Its classic linkage set (straight-line linkages, quick-return, Scotch yoke) overlaps DMG-Lib, KMODDL and Wikipedia. A 2022 conference paper on the site appears in the IATED library (abstract page could not be opened) [uncertain]
